blocks.explanation:
Logarithmic times trigonometric; \(\cos x\) is the derivative of \(\sin x\).
Plan: \(\ln(\sin x)\) first, \(\cos x\) second; the new integral reduces to \(\int \cos x\,dx\).
steps:
Given: \(\int \ln(\sin x)\cos x\,dx\), \(\sin x > 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: integration by parts with \(f(x) = \ln(\sin x)\), \(g(x) = \cos x\).

Integrate the second, differentiate the first
\[\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln(\sin x) = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\]
Why: chain rule: derivative of \(\ln u\) is \(\frac{u'}{u}\).

Apply integration by parts
\[= \ln(\sin x)\cdot\sin x - \int \sin x\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx\]
\[= \sin x\ln(\sin x) - \int \cos x\,dx\]
Why: \(\sin x\) cancels inside the integral.

Integrate
\[= \sin x\ln(\sin x) - \sin x + c\]
Why: \(\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x\ln(\sin x) - \sin x)\]
\[= \cos x\ln(\sin x) + \sin x\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \cos x\]
\[= \cos x\ln(\sin x)\]
Why: product rule; the \(\cos x\) terms cancel.
